title: 天堂私服 | 客戶端idx、pak說明
claims: IDX is described as an index/catalog for entries stored in matching client resource packages
PAK is described as the resource container; tools can use the index to list named resources and preview/extract entries
the article distinguishes Sprite, Text and Tile package families and associates them with different resource types
technical_details: opening an IDX as text can expose entry names such as 10306-24.spr
the article lists Sprite/Sprite00..Sprite15 packages with SPR/TBT/PNG/IMG-like resources
Text packages are associated with HTML/TBL and list.spr/list.spz
Tile packages are associated with TIL/XML
one demonstrated SPR preview/export produced an animation with nine image frames
procedures: open matching package with a resource tool
preview or extract selected resource rather than decoding everything
limitations: evidence is from Lineage 3.81C-era client material
some package/type descriptions are explicitly marked uncertain by the author
project_relevance: direct evidence for index-first resource inventory and source provenance
supports keeping SPR, icon, text/dialog and tile/XML resource classes distinct
verify: map actual 8.8 IDX/PAK families and entry types
verify package precedence and whether the same logical ID can exist in multiple packages

title: 天堂私服 | 補丁副檔名對應說明
claims: the article separates animation SPR, icon TBT, dialog HTML, configuration XML, UI IMG and text TBL roles
list.spr/list.spz are described as carrying action/image-count style definitions, with list.spz encrypted in the examined client
HTML is tied to NPC dialog interaction while XML examples include effectlist.xml and polymorphlist.xml
technical_details: list.ico is described as an upper-bound/icon-code related file in the old client
weapon example says invgfx=1 maps to 0.tbt while an armor example says invgfx=10 maps to 10.tbt; this inconsistency is preserved rather than normalized
effectlist.xml is named in relation to effect/status presentation
npc dialog example references server-side normal_action and client HTML
procedures: identify logical asset type before choosing resolver
trace server/NPC action name to client HTML where applicable
trace icon ID to TBT independently from animation SPR

article does not provide a complete magic/status icon mapping
invgfx/TBT examples contain a potential off-by-one or source inconsistency and must be verified instead of corrected
project_relevance: strong evidence that item icons and monster SPRs require separate resolvers
supports UI/dialog/resource chain and morph/effect configuration research
conflicts: source examples do not establish a single universal invgfx-to-TBT offset rule
verify: 8.8 HTML/dialog resource lookup and action dispatch
